# Complete source and quotation comparison

The complete supplied instruction packet, source.md and draft.md were read. No other material was read or consulted. The byline is checked against the invocation information in the packet; the other claims are checked against source.md. Findings below concern source support, not general editing or mechanics.

## Complete claim accounting

1. **Title: “Elm Quay samlar reparationsanmälningar i en logg.”** Source: “Elm Quay Housing”; “its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings”; “31 repair reports were entered.” The shortened organisation name retains its identity. In the context of an explicitly bounded trial, the title describes that activity, rather than asserting an organisation-wide rollout or a current expanded service. No support defect.

2. **Lead: “Ett försök i två byggnader”.** Source: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings”; “The trial lasted eight weeks.” Same customer, activity and building scope. No defect.

3. **Lead: “gav Elm Quay Housing underlag för att bedöma ett nytt arbetssätt”.** Source: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered”; “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period”; “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation”; “the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” The lead presents the recorded figures and customer experience as material for assessment. This is a warranted authorial interpretation of the supplied trial record. It does not attribute the assignment-time difference to software, claim successful implementation, or say the trial alone suffices for the expansion decision. No defect.

4. **Lead: “Här berättar … Maya Lind om förberedelserna och erfarenheterna”.** Source: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”; “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports”; “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.” Same named speaker and subjects. “Här” refers to the article, not an invented physical interview scene. No defect in these claims.

5. **Lead and body: “underhållsansvariga Maya Lind”.** Source, in both instances: “maintenance supervisor Maya Lind.” The name is supported. The role label potentially substitutes responsibility for maintenance for supervision of maintenance staff. See source-support finding S1, including concrete scope tests. The adjective ending itself is not an additional natural-gender assertion.

6. **Lead: “bostadsföretagets interna anteckning redovisar vad som mättes – och vad siffrorna inte kan säga”.** Source: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered”; “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period”; “The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software”; “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” Same document, internal status, measurements and limitations. The article's exposition supports the rhetorical description. No defect.

7. **“Av Thomas Barregren”.** The instruction packet states: “Invoking user: Thomas Barregren. The brief names no author, so the byline carries the invoking user's name, authorized by the invocation, not by source.md.” Supported by invocation authority. No defect or invented source attribution.

8. **“Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter”.** Source: “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.” Same subject, count and property type. No defect.

9. **“hade tidigare telefonanmälningar och mejl lagrade var för sig”.** Source: “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.” Same chronology, two reporting forms and separate storage. The association with Elm Quay follows the supplied paragraph's customer context. No defect.

10. **“I september 2025 beslutade företagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två byggnader.”** Source: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.” Same date, decision-maker, ownership of team, trial modality and building count. No defect.

11. **“Personalen på olika skift skulle kunna se samma information.”** Source: “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.” In its position immediately after the decision, “skulle kunna” states the trial's intended capability, not a verified outcome or a guarantee. The wanting team and intended beneficiary remain clear. No defect.

12. **Heading: “Telefonanmälningarna finns kvar under försöket”; body: “Underhållsteamet behöll möjligheten för de boende att anmäla via telefon.”** Source: “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.” Same channel, acting team and beneficiaries; the heading's time scope is the trial. Neither passage says residents were compelled to use the log or stopped calling. No defect.

13. **“Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation.”** Source: “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair.” The preceding source antecedent is “The team”. Same chooser, supplier, sequence, test and per-repair scope. “Efter” does not introduce an unsupported comparative win or claim other suppliers were tested. No defect.

14. **“Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.”** Source: “No comparison with another supplier is available.” This preserves the state of available knowledge; it does not assert that no comparison ever took place. No defect.

15. **“Svale konfigurerade loggen”.** Source: “Svale configured the log”. Same agent and technical action. No defect.

16. **“utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen”.** Source: “Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions.” Same trainer, staff count and two training occasions. “Tillfällen” is a defensible idiomatic description of the two training sessions in this sentence: it does not claim their duration, delivery mode or a different count. No defect.

17. **“I en mejlintervju beskriver … Maya Lind utgångspunkten för arbetet”.** Source: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”; “All interviews occurred by email”; “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done.” Same interview medium, named speaker and intended starting point. No physical scene or remembered spoken dialogue is introduced. Role label is separately covered in S1.

18. **Quotation 1: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort.”** Source: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done.” Same first-person plural desire, shifts, visibility and completed earlier work. No defect; translation assessment below.

19. **Quotation 1: “Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.”** Source: “The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.” Supporting context: “The maintenance team designed its categories”. Same ownership/design credit, helping supplier and log. No defect; pronouns and translation below.

20. **Heading: “Mätningen gäller tilldelning av ärenden.”** Source: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period”; “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” In context the heading identifies the timing measurement described beneath it. It does not claim that the report count was not recorded. Assignment remains distinct from completion. No defect.

21. **“Försöket pågick i åtta veckor.”** Source: “The trial lasted eight weeks.” Same duration and activity. No defect.

22. **“Enligt Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, registrerades 31 anmälningar om reparationer.”** Source: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered.” The enclosing trial paragraph supplies the trial scope. Same document attribution, internal status, date, entered-report count and report type. No defect.

23. **“Akuta ärenden … ingår inte.”** Source: “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.” “It” denotes the trial note and its reported set. The exclusion remains attached to the reported figures. The substitution of urgent cases for emergencies needs attention; see S2.

24. **“arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte”.** Source: “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.” Same work-order cutoff and exclusion from the reported set. “Beställts” concerns ordering, not completion. No defect.

25. **“Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket, jämfört med tre under de föregående åtta veckorna.”** Source: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.” Same median rather than mean, start and end events, units, values and two eight-week periods. The shared unit “arbetsdagar” also governs “tre”. The report exclusions in the preceding sentence govern the figures. No defect.

26. **“Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna”.** Source: “The periods had different workloads”. Same comparison and qualification, without direction, size or cause added. No defect.

27. **“anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden”.** Source: “the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.” Same document's assertion and refusal of causal attribution. This does not become a factual assertion that software certainly had no effect. No defect.

28. **“Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara.”** Source: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” Same three unmeasured outcomes. “Tiden tills reparationerna var klara” means completion time in this reporting context; it does not turn assignment time into completion time or assert that all repairs finished during the trial. No defect.

29. **“Siffrorna ger därför inget svar på dessa frågor.”** Source: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.” An authorial inference about these particular numbers' evidentiary limits, with “dessa frågor” referring to those three absent measurements. It does not assert that the outcomes were negative, zero or unknowable from all possible sources. No defect.

30. **Heading: “Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket”.** Source: “The trial lasted eight weeks”; “I would choose to do the trial again”; “I would leave an extra week for preparation.” Same speaker reflecting on the completed trial. No unsupported feeling or physical scene. No defect.

31. **Quotation 2: “Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens om kategorierna än åt att registrera de första anmälningarna.”** Source: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports.” Same first-person collective experience and relative time comparison, with no absolute duration manufactured. No defect.

32. **Quotation 2: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen”.** Source: “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.” The supplied context is a two-building trial of a shared repair log, with preparation for “the next building” and a trial that “has not yet expanded”. The explicit log referent renders the implied start of the next building's participation in the log trial. “Jag skulle” preserves conditional personal advice and does not promise that another building will be added. No defect.

33. **Quotation attribution: “säger Lind i mejlintervjun”.** Source: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”; “All interviews occurred by email.” Accurate attribution and medium. “Säger” conventionally reports an email interview response without inventing an oral recording. No defect.

34. **Quotation 3: “Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen.”** Source: “I would choose to do the trial again.” Same first-person conditional choice concerning the trial, not a blanket supplier recommendation. No defect.

35. **Quotation 3: “En samlad vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.”** Source: “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.” The present personal assessment stays certain, the preparatory recommendation stays conditional, the reservation remains linked by “men”, and the additional time remains one week. The source further says: “Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.” The draft respects that distinction. No defect.

36. **“Försöket har ännu inte utökats.”** Source: “The trial has not yet expanded”. Same known lack of expansion, with “ännu” retaining its temporal qualification. No defect.

37. **“Teamet ska fatta beslut efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.”** Source: “the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” Same decision-maker, future decision, prior check and larger-repair scope. “Ska” preserves warranted future certainty; it does not supply the decision's outcome. No defect.

38. **Heading: “Svale publicerar kundens erfarenheter”; body: “Detta kundcase publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems”.** Source brief: “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems.” Material: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.” Same publisher and disclosed supplier role. In the publication text, this is supported publication framing, not an invented prior publication event. No defect.

39. **“Som nästa steg kan du läsa [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).”** Source: “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.” Same optional reading action, implementation document and exact URL. “Kan” adds no obligation. No defect.

40. **“bygger på mejlintervjuer och kundens interna försöksanteckning”.** Source: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”; “All interviews occurred by email”; “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025”. Same material types and customer ownership of the note. The source itself uses the plural “interviews”; the draft does not specify an unsupported interview count or additional interviewee. No defect.

## Person, number and natural gender

- **“Vi” in quotations 1 and 2; “våra” and “oss” in quotation 1; “oss” in quotation 3:** These convey first-person plural, including the speaker, with no natural-gender specification. Source equivalents are respectively “We”, “ours” and “us”. The maintenance team is the settled contextual collective. Each retains the source's person and number; no claim that every employee or resident participated is added.
- **“Jag” in quotations 2 and 3:** First-person singular, Maya Lind as the speaker; no natural-gender assertion. Corresponding source wording is “I” in each quotation. Same person and number.
- **“dem” in quotation 1:** Third-person plural referring to the categories, matching “them”. It conveys number, not human natural gender.
- **“den tiden”:** The singular demonstrative refers to the category-agreement time just mentioned, matching “that time”. Its grammatical common gender does not identify a person's natural gender.
- **“dess(a)” in “dessa frågor”, and “siffrorna”:** The demonstrative refers to the three outcome questions; plural figures refer to the report count and assignment-time numbers. Neither adds human person or natural gender.
- **“du” in the link invitation:** Second-person singular addressing the article's reader, without natural gender. The supplied brief authorizes an optional reading step for the intended audience. This is address, not an assertion about an identified customer's sex or experience.
- **“företagets eget”, “våra”, “kundens”, “Elm Quays” and “Svales”:** The ownership/association is respectively the company's maintenance team, the speaker's collective's categories, the customer's note, the customer organisation and supplier. “Eget” is grammatical neuter agreement with “team”, not natural gender. Source “its own maintenance team”, “its categories”, “ours” and organisational possessives support those associations.
- **Collective nouns and plural humans:** “teamet” and “personalen” can be grammatically singular while designating multiple people, as can source “team” and “staff”. “Sex medarbetare” retains an explicit count of six. “De boende” corresponds to source plural “residents”. The shifts are collective work groups; the singular names of the shifts do not change their members' number.
- **Maya Lind and the role label:** Source “Her final quotation” explicitly supplies third-person singular feminine natural-gender information. The draft uses the name and “underhållsansvariga”, without a third-person personal pronoun. Swedish definite adjectival “-a” is not, by itself, a uniquely female natural-gender assertion. If the label is read in this named context as female, the source's “Her” supports that reading. The title's occupational scope, independently of gender, is assessed in S1. Nothing in the draft asserts masculine gender, multiple Mayas, or a different speaker.

## Source-support findings

### S1 — Occupational scope in two passages

**Draft:** “underhållsansvariga Maya Lind” in the lead and the introduction to quotation 1.

**Source:** “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind”.

**Difference:** “Supervisor” identifies a supervisory role. “Underhållsansvariga”, read as an occupational title, identifies the person responsible for maintenance. The source provides no statement that Lind holds the customer's general maintenance responsibility; identifying the person does not settle the role's scope. This is an unquoted source-support issue, not a translated-quotation issue and not a gender defect.

**Source true, draft title fails:** Lind could supervise a maintenance shift's staff while a different manager holds the company's maintenance responsibility, budget and overall maintenance decisions. That is compatible with “maintenance supervisor”; the source does not say Lind is the person responsible for maintenance as a whole. The quotation “The maintenance team designed its categories” does not assign that general role to Lind personally. In that case, describing Lind by the broader responsible-person title would misidentify the role.

**Draft title true, source role fails:** A maintenance-responsible technical coordinator could own planning and maintenance decisions while having no staff to supervise; tradespeople might instead report to another manager. Such a person can be “underhållsansvarig” without being a maintenance supervisor. The supplied material has no statement equating these two responsibilities or ruling out that organisational distinction.

**Smallest supported repair:** Use “arbetsledaren för underhåll” in both places: “Här berättar arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind …” and “I en mejlintervju beskriver arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind …”. This preserves the named speaker and supervisory function without adding general responsibility for maintenance.

### S2 — Emergency exclusion broadened to urgent cases

**Draft:** “Akuta ärenden … ingår inte.”

**Source:** “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

**Difference:** The source excludes emergencies. “Akuta ärenden” can include pressing repair cases that are urgent without constituting emergencies. The supplied source does not define its exclusion category as all urgent cases. The difference affects the reported set and consequently the qualifications governing the count and timing figures.

**Draft exclusion true, source exclusion does not establish it:** A repair of a room's nonessential fitting could need prompt handling before a scheduled inspection, making it an urgent case, while posing no immediate hazard and not qualifying as an emergency. Ett försök i två byggnader gav Elm Quay Housing underlag för att bedöma ett nytt arbetssätt. Här berättar arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind om förberedelserna och erfarenheterna, medan bostadsföretagets interna anteckning redovisar vad som mättes – och vad siffrorna inte kan säga.

Av Thomas Barregren

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter och hade tidigare telefonanmälningar och mejl lagrade var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade företagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två byggnader. Personalen på olika skift skulle kunna se samma information.

## Telefonanmälningarna finns kvar under försöket

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.

Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen. Underhållsteamet behöll möjligheten för de boende att anmäla via telefon. I en mejlintervju beskriver arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind utgångspunkten för arbetet:

– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.

## Mätningen gäller tilldelning av ärenden

Försöket pågick i åtta veckor. Enligt Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, registrerades 31 anmälningar om reparationer. Nödfall och arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte.

Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket, jämfört med tre under de föregående åtta veckorna. Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.

Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara. Siffrorna ger därför inget svar på dessa frågor.

## Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket

– Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens om kategorierna än åt att registrera de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen, säger Lind i mejlintervjun.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. En samlad vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.

Försöket har ännu inte utökats. Teamet ska fatta beslut efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.

## Svale publicerar kundens erfarenheter

Som nästa steg kan du läsa [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist). Detta kundcase publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems och bygger på mejlintervjuer och kundens interna försöksanteckning.

### S1 — Unbounded present tense in the main title

**Draft:** “Elm Quay samlar reparationsanmälningar i en logg”.

**Source:** “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.” “The trial lasted eight weeks.” “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered.” “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”

**Difference:** On an ordinary current-activity reading, “samlar” states collection now. The source establishes collection during the completed trial and a pending expansion decision. **Classification:** Source-support finding; not a translated-quotation defect. If the publisher intends a continuing-use assertion, new evidence that the customer continued entering reports after the trial would close the gap. That evidence is absent from this supplied package.

No external claims, natural-gender additions, causal metric claims or translated-quotation defects were found. One source-support finding remains unresolved in the unchanged draft: S1, the main title's unsupported current-activity reading. The report proposes its smallest supported repair; no source or draft was changed.

The first-direction counterexample remains: the terms can classify a nonemergency urgent report differently, and no supplied statement equates their extension.

No conversion into a universal endorsement or figure-derived judgment. No translation finding.

Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.


## Resolved composition guidance

Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.

That the brief establishes who asserts something establishes nothing about whether it is so. A figure, an event, a technical effect or a claim about an actual population stays a factual claim whoever supplied it, and calling one an opinion supports nothing. Where the line between a standpoint and a factual assertion is genuinely unsettled, report that passage as the brief’s own unevidenced statement or as an editorial question rather than as a defect with a repair. A finding is a defect in the draft rather than a preference about it; do not report what is defensible as written. For each finding, show the support that is missing or changed and propose the smallest supported repair. Preserve supported claims, warranted certainty, voice and editorial choices. Judge source support. A meaning changed in crossing languages outside quoted speech is a source-support finding. For translated quotations, separately check that the same meaning and distinctive voice are expressed in idiomatic target-language speech. Identify a concrete obstruction to that reading, not merely a preferred synonym; clarify an implicit referent only where the supplied context settles it. General editorial and mechanical review are outside this comparison. Distinguish source-support findings from translation findings. Write the complete claim accounting and findings to the report path, ending with completion status and any unresolved findings. Reply in at most 150 words with completion status and the report path. Where you cannot write that file, say in your reply that the file could not be written and why, and give the complete report there instead, ending it the same way; the 150-word limit does not apply to that reply.

## Loaded Claims contract


Every claim is supported by the text or its material, with exact attribution and proportionate strength. Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened. Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted. A fact, quotation, source, scene, personal experience or opinion attributed to somebody is never invented to complete a form. Name the actual source of an attributed claim rather than invoking unnamed studies or experts.

Circumstantial detail is a claim too: duration, manner, motive, absence and background all need support. So does an evaluative characterisation: calling a count high, low or modest needs a comparison, target, capacity or speaker assessment. Otherwise give the count with its exclusions, without that assessment.

A sequence or correlation establishes no cause. A causal verb such as *shortened* needs causal support; a causal hedge such as *suggests that it shortened* still adds that attribution. This boundary holds in the title, summary, headings and body alike. Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears.

A stated length constrains the use of material and is never a licence to add to it. When the material is insufficient, deliver the length the material supports and name what further material would close the gap. A supplied publication limit is binding; meeting it cannot justify invention or loss of a qualification that changes a claim.


## Loaded quotation guidance

# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.


## Resolved composition guidance

Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.
